notes:
Tomasz was explicit: if only three fit this week, do his #1 (scale), #2 (where it concentrates), #3 (product vs process). I'm doing exactly those three tonight, and folding Tobias's overlapping asks into the same reports rather than spending extra slots: merchant clustering → tenant column in report 2 (each warehouse belongs to one tenant); shrinkage-vs-gain skew → signed net variance columns in reports 1 & 2; velocity/value materiality → velocity and value columns in report 3. I'm deferring Tomasz's #4 (reservation reliability) and #5 (dedicated trend) to a later night, though report 1's month grain gives a free first look at trend.

Definition check before committing: "physical count different from stock on record" should be measured from stock_movements where kind = 'cycle_count' — that's an enumerated, reliable code — rather than stock_adjustments.reason, which is free text with no fixed code list and reasons like "damage"/"shrinkage" aren't cycle-count-driven surprises, they're logged causes. I don't want the engineer guessing at string matches, so I'm specifying stock_movements.kind='cycle_count' as the source of truth for all three reports, and treating "count found less than system" (quantity<0) as shrinkage and "found more" (quantity>0) as overage.

Value is costed off supplier_products.unit_cost (preferred supplier, else cheapest active) rather than retail price, since write-off/valuation exposure (Tobias's framing) is a cost-basis question. All money converted to EUR via exchange_rates (base_code=EUR): value_eur = value_in_quote_currency / rate.

All three reports use the same 12-month window (2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, the last complete year) so they're comparable to each other.

requests.title: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
requests.question: How often do physical cycle counts come back different from the stock quantity we had on record, and how large are those differences in units and estimated value, across 2025?
columns: cycle_count_events (count of stock_movements rows with kind='cycle_count')
warehouses_affected (distinct warehouses with at least one cycle_count event that month)
units_short (sum of abs(quantity) where quantity<0, i.e. counted less than recorded)
units_over (sum of quantity where quantity>0, i.e. counted more than recorded)
net_units_variance (sum of signed quantity; negative = net shrinkage)
abs_units_variance (sum of abs(quantity), total magnitude of mismatch)
estimated_value_eur (sum of abs(quantity) * unit cost, converted to EUR)
requests.details: Source: stock_movements where kind='cycle_count', occurred_at between 2025-01-01 and 2025-12-31 inclusive, across all tenants/warehouses. Join stock_locations on stock_location_id to get warehouse_id for the distinct-warehouse count. Cost basis: join supplier_products on variant_id, preferring is_preferred=true; if no preferred row exists for a variant, use the lowest unit_cost among active (is_active=true) supplier_products rows for that variant; if a variant has no supplier_products row, exclude it from estimated_value_eur but still count it in unit/event columns (note the gap in the report notes). Convert supplier_products.currency_code amounts to EUR using exchange_rates (base_code='EUR', quote_code=that currency, as_of = date of stock_movements.occurred_at): value_eur = value_in_currency / rate. Round estimated_value_eur to whole EUR. Order by month ascending.

requests.title: Stock discrepancies by warehouse and location type
requests.question: Does the stock-count mismatch concentrate in particular warehouses, particular storage-location kinds (e.g. bulk shelving vs pick bins), or particular merchants, in a way that signals valuation/write-off exposure?
requests.grain: warehouse and stock-location kind (e.g. one row = one warehouse's 'bulk' locations, another = that warehouse's 'pick' locations)
columns: estimated_value_eur (abs variance costed and converted to EUR, same method as report 1)
share_of_total_value_pct (this row's estimated_value_eur / sum of estimated_value_eur across all rows, *100, rounded 1dp)
requests.details: Same source and window as 'Scale of stock count discrepancies by month': stock_movements kind='cycle_count', occurred_at in 2025-01-01..2025-12-31. Join stock_locations (for kind and warehouse_id), warehouses (name, tenant_id), tenants (name). Cost/FX conversion identical to report 1 (supplier_products preferred-then-cheapest unit_cost, converted via exchange_rates). Group by tenant, warehouse, location_kind. Order by estimated_value_eur descending, tie-break by abs_units_variance descending, then tenant_name, warehouse_name, location_kind for determinism. Cap at 50 rows (top 50 by value) and note total distinct warehouse/location-kind combinations found in the data even if more than 50 exist.
builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month

requests.title: Stock discrepancies by product category: handling vs tracking-method issue
requests.question: Are stock-count discrepancies spread evenly across product categories, or concentrated in certain categories, lot/serial-tracked items, or high-velocity items — pointing to a handling problem vs a tracking-method problem?
columns: pct_events_lot_or_serial_tracked (% of this category's cycle_count events where stock_movements.lot_id is not null)
avg_monthly_units_sold (velocity proxy: total order_items.quantity for variants in this category, orders placed in 2025, divided by 12, rounded 1dp)

variance_per_1000_units_sold (abs_units_variance / (avg_monthly_units_sold*12) * 1000, rounded 1dp; normalizes discrepancy by sales volume so high-velocity categories aren't automatically flagged just for having more activity)
requests.details: Source: stock_movements where kind='cycle_count', occurred_at in 2025-01-01..2025-12-31, joined to product_variants (variant_id) -> products (product_id) -> categories (primary_category_id) for category_name; treat variants whose product has no primary_category_id as a single 'Uncategorized' row. Lot/serial-tracked flag: stock_movements.lot_id is not null on the cycle_count row itself. Velocity: order_items joined to product_variants on product_variant_id, orders.placed_at in 2025-01-01..2025-12-31, status not in ('cancelled'), summed by the variant's category. Cost/FX conversion identical to report 1. Order by estimated_value_eur descending, tie-break by category_name. Expect well under 50 rows (category count is small); if it is large due to deep category trees, group only by the product's primary_category (no rollup to parent).
builds_on: Scale of stock count discrepancies by month
